caption: The drawing consists of a square-shaped textile pattern featuring an arrangement of geometric shapes and motifs. The primary colors used in the composition are red and blue. Red is the dominant color and appears as closely-packed ovals and small circular forms arranged in repeated patterns, filling most of the space within the square. Blue serves as the background and forms a grid-like network throughout the pattern, dividing the red motifs into organized sections. The center area has a diamond-shaped formation composed of smaller diamond clusters, oriented in a cross-like arrangement that radiates toward the edges of the square. At each corner of the square are four large rectangular sections, densely filled with the same red oval motifs set against the blue grid. The overall effect is a complex, symmetrical, and highly organized pattern. The drawing is set on a plain off-white background, and a small, handwritten text appears in the lower right corner.
title: Coverlet
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
